executive_assessment.text: Ribeira Afonso, Malanza, Neves and historical Lembá/Príncipe impacts provide local evidence; modelled flood losses are conditional projections, not observed future losses.
Água Grande's inclusive scorecard work is a planning input. Proposed drainage, watershed and water-security measures remain unverified implementation.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2025-08-29 reports: UNICEF identifies rainy-season flood, landslide, erosion and drought exposure in mountainous and riverside areas, naming Ribeira Afonso, Malanza and Neves as disproportionately affected.

Source dated 2025-08-29 reports: After December 2021 floods, Lembá District recorded 2,104 people affected and two child deaths; damage included bridges, a water plant, crops, fishing boats and over half of latrines.

Source dated 2025-08-29 reports: After May 2024 floods damaged Príncipe infrastructure and livelihoods, UNICEF reports launching support for over 7,400 families within 72 hours and mobilizing an estimated US$475,000.

Source dated 2024-05-02 reports: The assessment identifies Malanza and Santa Catarina among the most affected subdistricts; about 18,500 people are flood-affected annually on average under present-climate conditions.
Source dated 2024-05-02 reports: World Bank feature interviews portray recurrent flood and wave damage as a livelihood concern for a fisherwoman in Praia Cruz and a fish trader in Praia Abade.

Source dated 2026-10-06 reports: Água Grande District convened more than 20 cross-sector representatives in September 2026 to assess urban risk, including gender and disability organizations, civil protection and meteorological services.

Source dated 2026-10-06 reports: Participants used the city resilience scorecard to agree priority gaps and draft objectives and coordination arrangements; UNDRR says a full district strategy and action plan remain future work.
Source dated 2026-10-06 reports: Água Grande’s tourism director said flooding and coastal erosion expose tourism, while the existing tourism development plan does not address disaster risk.

Source dated not stated reports: UNDP’s project page describes climate-driven urban flooding and water-system turbidity affecting São Tomé and Santo António, with interruptions for about one-third of the population and added water-collection burdens for women and girls.

Source dated not stated reports: The proposed package includes climate-resilient water, waste and drainage coordination, watershed management in Água Grande, priority drainage works, and water-quality monitoring in the Água Grande and Santo António basins.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification or human approval. 18 of 18 evidence records and 0 of 0 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
The 2024 national flood-risk assessment could not be inspected directly; flood-loss projections are cited through the 2026 NDC.
The possible maritime-crime pathway relies on Gulf of Guinea evidence from elsewhere; no local event or causal dataset was inspected.
Draft collection pending human source review and approval. IDA eligibility is not an FCV classification.
National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.
The bank contains no completed mediated climate-FCV pathway; this is an evidence gap, not evidence of absence.
Maritime-crime analogy from elsewhere in the Gulf of Guinea cannot establish local incidence.
No inspected primary source established a country-specific climate-to-conflict or violence pathway, or an FCV constraint on adaptation delivery; this remains a documented search gap.

The World Bank technical flood-risk PDF exceeded the web reader's 10 MB content limit. Its accessible author summary supports claims, but the report-index excerpt and summary disagreed on district percentages; percentages are omitted pending direct report review.
The 2026 Country Climate and Development Report is disclosed in Portuguese and was not fully reviewed in this extraction; no claims rely on it.
The accessible UNDP page presents project design and beneficiary estimates, and labels funding pipeline; it does not verify implementation, reach or outcomes.
UNDRR reports draft local strategy inputs for Água Grande, not an adopted district plan or completed resilience outcomes.
The UNICEF report is an operational situation report; its specific event statistics describe 2021 and 2024 shocks rather than current district risk prevalence.
UNICEF source's country subsection is printed p.14 but physical PDF p.15; main verified the cited named locations and historical figures.
No climate-to-violence pathway is added. Water burdens, governance gaps and a pipeline project do not themselves establish FCV causation.
Draft extension: human source review and approval remain pending. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
